neighbours.label: plural nouns naming a class of goods that is held, grown or carried, strongest on ' drugs', ' crops' and ' weapons' (weaker: ' movies', ' games', ' animals'); the singular is much weaker
fire: The clinic threw away the unused drugs at the end of each month.
With more rain the valley could grow enough crops to last the winter.
The guards searched every car for hidden weapons at the border.
The longer he sold drugs on that street, the more people knew his face.
Farmers along the river lost most of their crops in the flood.
The rebels bought weapons from traders across the lake.
Many older patients keep spare drugs in a kitchen drawer.
The settlers planted crops on the hillside behind the fort.
quiet: The clinic threw away the unused paperwork at the end of each month.
With more rain the valley could stay green enough to last the summer.
The guards searched every car for a hidden passenger at the border.
The longer he sang on that street, the more people knew his face.
Farmers along the river lost most of their land in the flood.
The rebels bought time from traders across the lake.
Many older patients keep a spare key in a kitchen drawer.
The settlers planted a flag on the hillside behind the fort.

notes: Probes: drugs 0.52-0.75, crops 0.52, weapons 0.35, movies/games 0.21, animals 0.12, 'a weapon' 0.16, 'furniture and clothing' 0.03.
